rationale: Evidence: iteration 2 (kp 3.0, kd 0.4) scored 132.0 and iteration 3 (kp 2.5, kd 0.7) scored 122.2. Both kept the widened 5-sensor span (x = -0.06 to +0.06, y = 0.05, 16 mm footprint), which cut line-loss events from about 1.0 to 0.05-0.8. Every trial still ended off track at max_error about 0.06 m, the off-track limit, with RMS error about 0.03 m. Steering oscillation was 0.22-0.28 in the higher-gain runs and fell only slightly with lower kp, so the loop is overshooting and jittering rather than losing the line. The one oval finish came from the higher-kp run, so kp near 3 gives more useful authority. Iteration 3 changed kp and kd together, so it does not isolate kd. Changes: keep the iteration-2 geometry exactly so the controller is the only variable. Raise kp slightly from 2.5 to 2.8, which sits between the two tested gains and keeps the steering authority the oval finish needed. Raise kd from 0.7 to 1.0 to damp the fast signal changes behind the oscillation (the scored data show oscillation rising with kp, so extra damping is the most direct lever). Keep base_speed at 1.3, since higher speed would add lateral load before the oscillation is fixed, and keep ki at 0 to avoid windup on the bends. Expected result: steering oscillation below about 0.2, max_error held nearer the limit for longer, and progress above about 0.35 on the oval and s-bend. Finishing within 3 s is still uncertain and will need a speed increase once the robot stays on the line. The telemetry should confirm whether kd suppresses the jitter without costing progress.
